page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2ne.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. It features 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs via hyperthreading, backed by 64.0 GB of system memory, which provides a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. A key hardware feature is the inclusion of 1919 GB of bundled local SSD storage, alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the instance delivers modest compute performance. Single-core and multi-core CPU tests, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, place the processor in the bottom 25% tier. Similarly, memory bandwidth for small blocks is weak, though large block read and write operations perform at an average level. Cryptographic and compression tasks, such as single-threaded gzip, show poor performance, landing in the bottom 10%. However, the instance maintains average performance in Passmark CPU tests and small-model LLM inference tasks.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.i2ne.2xlarge is its lower compute efficiency relative to its storage and memory capacity. While raw CPU-bound processing is limited, the combination of 64 GB of RAM and nearly 2 TB of local SSD storage makes this instance highly resource-dense for storage-centric workloads. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for scenarios requiring high local data retention and moderate memory footprints, such as relational databases, caching layers, and local file processing, rather than compute-heavy or high-throughput web serving.

Operating on the KVM hypervisor, it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Benchmark evaluations reveal a clear tradeoff: while raw compute metrics from Geekbench and stress-ng fall into the bottom 25%, large-block memory bandwidth and Passmark CPU scores remain average. It is best suited for database hosting, caching systems, and local data processing tasks that prioritize storage capacity and memory density over high-performance compute capabilities.
